name: Untertilliach
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny, secluded village in the upper Gailtal, with authentic nature and absolute tranquility.
beschreibung:
Untertilliach lies at 1,180 meters above sea level in the upper Gailtal, in Bezirk Lienz in Osttirol, not far from the Italian border. The village has around 250 inhabitants and is one of the most remote settlements in the Austrian Alpine region. Anyone who comes here deliberately leaves the main routes behind – the narrow road almost ends here, and the Karnischen Alpen close in from all sides.

The surroundings invite extended hikes on the Gailtaler Höhenweg, which passes directly by the village and continues across the border toward the south. In summer, countless alpine pastures stretch across the high plateaus; in winter, Untertilliach remains largely spared from ski tourism – silence and pristine mountain landscape shape the scene. The parish church St. Margaretha with its late-Gothic winged altar is one of the village's cultural gems. Anyone who experiences the Gailtal up here immediately senses why the region is regarded by those in the know as an insider tip for nature-focused getaways: no through traffic, no lift facilities, only meadows, forest, and the constant murmur of the Gail.

Culinarily, the village thrives on simple, down-to-earth cuisine of Osttirol – Kasnudeln, Graukäse, and regional game dishes are on the menu in the few inns. Untertilliach is not a place for quick visits, but for all who deliberately seek distance from everyday life and appreciate the slowness of the mountains.
